what: Place the Ingenuity flight-26 nadir mosaic (40 frames, ~17 m across, backshell + debris + rock field) in HiRISE ESP_068294 and use it as centimetre-scale truth.
mosaic: 40 downward frames chained by SIFT+RANSAC homographies (38 of 39 pairs with >=20 inliers). Scale from the nominal 8 m / 294 px = 0.027 m per pixel.

attempts.method: pixel correlation, backshell anchored, rotation 0-359 deg, scale 0.022-0.033, both chiralities
attempts.verdict: rejected: best scale at the edge of the search range, margin over the alternative only 0.064

attempts.method: two shared objects: backshell + a debris piece 4.2 m NW in HiRISE / 156 px in the mosaic
attempts.independent_check_matches_of_other_objec: 0 of 20 (chance: mean 0.9, 95th percentile 2, best of 360 rotations 4)
attempts.verdict: not validated: the other mosaic objects are mostly rocks < 0.5 m, invisible at 25 cm per pixel, so the check has little power; the pixel correlation gives it no support

attempts.method: long frame chain (101 frames, t = 59-139 s) to link the parachute to the backshell
attempts.verdict: invalid: across featureless dune stretches the matcher locks onto fixed camera features (helicopter shadow, lens marks) and returns zero motion, so the mosaic does not grow

attempts.method: motion-tracking fix: rectify the equidistant fisheye to a pinhole, remove the camera-fixed pattern, homography pose graph (scripts/ingenuity/track_flight_h.py)
attempts.result: frames chained into one consistent group: 97 (idx 64-160), up from 38; 379 pairwise measurements, 282 kept, median residual 0.23 px; mosaic of the whole stretch about 75 x 60 m (results/ingenuity/strip_mosaic_97_frames.png)
attempts.root_cause_found: the camera is an equidistant fisheye (CAHVORE type 3, linearity 0, f = 275 px, 133 deg field of view); treating it as a pinhole broke plane homographies at wide angles, and fixed lens/shadow features made featureless-ground pairs look static
attempts.unresolved: per-step in-plane rotation bias of about -1.5 deg plus real yaw jumps of 25-29 deg: the absolute heading of the strip is not reliable

attempts.method: register the 97-frame strip to HiRISE: masked NCC over rotation/scale/mirror, no location prior, fine and coarse band
attempts.result: no distinct peak: coarse band best 0.392 vs 99th percentile 0.377 of all placements, second distinct mode 0.389; every top placement puts the mosaic's backshell ~35 m from the real one

attempts.method: heading from the helicopter's shadow and a computed sun position (Ls 212, elevation 58 deg, azimuth 170 deg)
attempts.result: predicted shadow offset at 8 m: 5.0 m; measured median 4.3 m (consistent). The per-frame direction check was inconclusive because the detector was confined to the mean shadow position while the helicopter yaws.
camera model built from the metadata (f = 1780 px, strong radial term R1 = 0.47, round-trip error up to 0.013 normalised units after damped inversion); structure from motion not yet run

attempts.method: colour-frame photogrammetry: SIFT + essential matrix + incremental SfM + BA (scripts/ingenuity/sfm_rte.py); then orthorectification onto a nominal ground plane (rte_ortho.py)
attempts.result: only 1 of 45 image pairs verified (30 inliers) in raw frames; after orthorectification consecutive pairs gave 4-14 similarity inliers. Low-contrast ground, grazing views and large yaw/baseline changes defeat feature matching. No multi-view reconstruction.

attempts.method: sun-derived heading for the backshell stretch (frames 133-154): helicopter shadow with a computed sun (azimuth 170, elevation 58) and rock-shadow direction

result.helicopter_shadow: rotation of the mosaic to north-up -28.6 deg (clockwise-positive), i.e. 28.6 deg counter-clockwise in OpenCV terms; per-frame MAD 16 deg
result.rock_shadows: direction toward the sun -16.5 deg in the mosaic frame (MAD 33 deg) -> 264 deg counter-clockwise
result.length_check: helicopter shadow offset 150-160 px vs 172 px expected from the sun elevation: consistent

attempts.verdict: noisy; the two physical headings disagree with each other by about 50 deg

attempts.method: local registration of the backshell neighbourhood (+-5 m and +-8 m patches), translation pinned to the backshell, rotation 0-359 and scale scanned (scripts/ingenuity/register_local.py)
attempts.verdict: a coherent peak at 210-214 deg (neighbours 208-218 all high), consistent between two patch sizes, but only 0.06-0.07 above the second mode, it is the backshell blob that anchors it, and it contradicts the helicopter-shadow compass by exactly 180 deg and the rock-shadow compass by 50 deg. Visual overlay inconclusive. Not validated.

attempts.method: final: hand-read helicopter shadow positions (frames 136-154) -> shadow compass; fine registration on three independent HiRISE passes

result.shadow_compass: mosaic-to-north rotation 217 deg counter-clockwise, circular sd 12 deg, 6 frames
result.image_correlation: 208 deg, scale 0.0290 m/px, same translation (-0.4, +1.1) m in all three passes (068294, 068360, 068426)
result.earlier_contradiction: caused by an automatic shadow detector that locked onto rock shadows (180 deg off)

attempts.verdict: VALIDATED: two independent methods agree within 9 deg; scale equals the nominal 8 m / 275 px

conclusion: Placement validated for the backshell neighbourhood (rotation 211 deg ccw, scale 0.0290 m/px, translation (-0.4, +1.1) m). Used as truth in benchmark/object_final.py: see docs/METHODS.md 7c.
what_would_fix_it: Ground-plane motion from visual odometry with static-feature masking, or the 10 colour frames (oblique, both objects) with a photogrammetric solution, or a larger shared structure than the backshell and one piece.
